tasks.title: Memory importance scoring at write time
tasks.description: Initial strength should reflect memory importance rather than always defaulting to 1.0. The Codex extraction prompt should score each memory 1-5 by type (decision=5, preference=4, feedback=4, pattern=3, fact=2 as defaults). Map score to initial strength in the 0.6-1.0 range so high-signal memories decay slower from birth. Patch addMemory() and addMemories() in lib/memory.js to accept an importance field and set initial strength accordingly. Update the Codex extraction prompt in extractSessionToKnowledge() to request and return importance scores alongside each memory.

tasks.title: Memory consolidation synthesis — deduplication on write
tasks.description: Before writing new memories from Codex extraction, compare each candidate against existing project memories using Jaccard similarity on tags plus substring overlap on content. Merge near-duplicates (similarity above 0.7) by reinforcing the existing memory rather than creating a new document. Prevents the collection from filling with restatements of the same facts across sessions. Fetch existing memories once per extraction batch, score all candidates against them, and split candidates into new writes vs reinforcements before committing.

tasks.title: Memory editing and correction UI
tasks.description: Provide a path for Scott to flag, edit, or manually archive a specific memory. Codex misextractions currently persist until natural decay (weeks). A Polaris panel listing memories by project with inline edit and archive controls closes the human feedback loop on extraction quality. The panel should show content, type, tags, strength, accessCount, and age. Editing a memory resets its strength to the importance-based initial value; archiving sets _archived: true immediately.

tasks.title: Experience-to-skill distillation — higher-order memory consolidation synthesis
tasks.description: A weekly Codex pass clusters episodic memories by semantic similarity, identifies repeated patterns across them, and writes a single consolidated higher-order memory in their place. For example, 20 individual observations about tool choices synthesize into one durable preference memory. Original episodic memories are archived after synthesis. Implements the PowerMem two-layer experience plus skill architecture. Should run as a routine session on a weekly cron, fire-and-forget, with results logged to the server log.

tasks.title: Cross-project memory tier
tasks.description: Add a global memory tier alongside project-scoped memories. Memories tagged with project: global are returned in searchMemories calls for any project. Supports facts that are true across all projects: code style preferences, tool preferences, personal working patterns, recurring feedback. Prevents duplication of the same preference memory in every project collection. Requires a Firestore query change to OR-filter on project == requested OR project == global.

tasks.title: Forgetting curve calibration by memory type
tasks.description: Current decay constants (STABILITY_BASE=7 days, DECAY_THRESHOLD=0.1) are uniform across all memory types. Preferences and decisions should decay slower than facts and observations — a preference is more stable than an incidental observation. Once the collection has enough retrieval history, tune stability multipliers per type. Long-term: use retrieval outcome signals (did the session act on this memory?) to adjust decay rate per document individually.

tasks.title: Bi-temporal audit log schema for security tooling (design constraint)
tasks.description: Forward reference and design constraint for future Polaris security tools. Any security audit log system built on top of the memory/knowledge infrastructure must use bi-temporal structure: valid_time (when the fact was true in the real world) and transaction_time (when Polaris recorded it). This enables forensic past-state reconstruction: given an arbitrary past moment T, reconstruct exactly what the system knew and what was true, independently. Critical for answering Were we secure at T vs Did we think we were secure at T -- a meaningful distinction for CMMC, HIPAA, and SOC2 compliance. Compound condition detection: graph traversal over bi-temporal edges can find attack windows where multiple conditions overlapped (e.g. suspended account + live access edge = breach window during interval [T1, T2]). Schema sketch: { entityId, attribute, value, validFrom, validTo, txFrom, txTo }. Do not build this as a flat log -- the temporal indexing is load-bearing.

tasks.title: Isolate backlog writes from the shared primary repo (concurrency hazard)
tasks.description: Multiple parallel sessions edit docs/backlog.json in the shared primary repo (C:\Users\scott\Code\Polaris) on main at the same time. During task #51 planning, an uncommitted backlog edit was swept into another session's commit (ccf9278) and the working tree briefly showed tasks from 3+ sessions at once (in-flight #56/#59). Fix: backlog reads/writes performed by skills (plan-task, start-build, finish-build, status transitions) should operate in an isolated worktree pinned to a freshly-fetched origin/main, mutate atomically, and push HEAD:main with rebase-on-reject — never edit the shared primary working tree directly. Prevents lost/misattributed backlog changes and task-number collisions.

tasks.title: Orchestrator skill: multi-session conflict detection
tasks.description: Build /orchestrate — a universal Claude Code skill that monitors open PRs across all active sessions for a project, detects file-set intersections, classifies conflict types (additive / same-line / correctness divergence), and writes merger guides to Obsidian. Invoked automatically when a second session opens on the same project. General-first with per-project config block.

objective.statement: Provide Scott with automatic cross-session visibility into file-set conflicts between parallel build sessions, so conflicts are detected before PR review rather than at merge time.
successCriteria: Orchestrator session auto-spawns with title "Project Orchestrator" when a project reaches 2 active sessions
Orchestrator session auto-closes when the last session on a project closes
Init builds file-set watch list for all active branches, including branches with no open PR
Monitor loop refreshes watch list on new commits before running intersection check
Burst GIT:COMMITS events within one tick window are debounced to a single analysis run
File-set intersection triggers conflict classification and merger guide written to Obsidian
Dependency-violation alert fires when a task starts before its blocking PR is merged
Orchestrator card displays amber-gold pulsing glow, absent on all other session cards
nonGoals: Full orchestrator status panel in UI

tasks.plan:
## Overview

Build /orchestrate: a universal Claude Code skill that monitors all active session branches for a
project, detects file-set intersections between branches, classifies conflict types (additive /
same-line / correctness-divergence), and writes merger guides to Obsidian. Auto-spawned by server.js
as a dedicated chat session when a project reaches 2 active sessions; torn down when the last session closes.

## Phases

Phase 0: Spike -- validate spawnMaxChat auto-invocation mechanism
Phase 1: server.js orchestrator lifecycle (per-project session-count map, spawn at 2, teardown at 0,
         dedup guard, title "Project Orchestrator")
Phase 2: orchestrate.md scaffold + init (CLAUDE.md startup, gh pr list, git diff watch list, gh failure handling)
Phase 3: Monitor loop (health monitor pattern, 30s default, collect-and-flush debounce,
         GIT:COMMITS refresh, BACKLOG:CHANGED dep check, REGISTRY:CHANGED note)
Phase 4: Conflict classification engine (additive / same-line / correctness-divergence via git diff deep read)
Phase 5: Output artifacts + UI (status table, merger guide to Obsidian, dep-violation alert,
         mockup.html amber-gold pulsing glow CSS 2.5s)
Phase 6: Fixture branches + end-to-end proof run

## First Proof Unit

Open a second session on any project; "Project Orchestrator" session card with pulsing amber-gold
glow appears within 2s. Verified via manual observation in Polaris UI.

proofUnits.title: Orchestrator spawns on second session open
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: When a second session opens on the same project, a session card titled Project Orchestrator with pulsing glow appears.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Launch Polaris, project = Polaris. (2) Open first session. (3) Open second session on same project. (4) Observe: Project Orchestrator card appears.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: No orchestrator card; session-count logic not yet in server.js.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Project Orchestrator card visible within 2s of second session launch.

proofUnits.title: Orchestrator closes when last session closes
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: When the last build session on a project closes, the orchestrator session also closes and its card disappears.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Two sessions + orchestrator open on Polaris. (2) Close one build session: orchestrator stays. (3) Close second: orchestrator card disappears.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Orchestrator stays open after all build sessions close (leak).
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Orchestrator card gone within 3s of last session close.

proofUnits.title: Init builds file set for branch with no open PR
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Watch list includes file sets built from git diff directly for branches with no open PR.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Create local branch test-no-pr touching server.js, no PR opened. (2) Launch orchestrator. (3) Confirm server.js in watch list for test-no-pr in status table.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: test-no-pr missing from watch list (only PR branches tracked).
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Init status table shows test-no-pr with server.js in its file set.

proofUnits.title: gh failure surfaces error and asks for next steps
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: gh failure at init prints the exact error and asks Scott whether to continue in git-only mode or halt.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) gh auth logout. (2) Launch orchestrator. (3) Observe init output for error message and prompt.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Orchestrator silently skips PR metadata or hangs.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Init shows exact gh error + prompt: Continue in git-only mode or halt?
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A -- restore gh auth after test.

proofUnits.title: Watch list refreshes after new commit on a branch
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: After a new commit lands on branch-a, the next tick refreshes branch-a file set before running intersection check.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Orchestrator running with branch-a touching file X. (2) Commit change to file Y on branch-a. (3) Wait for next tick. (4) File Y appears in branch-a file set in status table.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: File Y not in watch list after commit (stale list from init).
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Status table shows file Y in branch-a file set on the next tick.

proofUnits.title: Debounce collapses burst events to one analysis run
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Three GIT:COMMITS events arriving within one tick window produce exactly one conflict analysis run.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Set interval to 10s. (2) Push three rapid commits to a watched branch within one window. (3) Count conflict-check log entries in orchestrator output for that tick.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Three separate conflict analysis runs logged for the same tick.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Exactly one conflict-check entry in orchestrator log for that tick.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A -- reset interval to 30s after test.

proofUnits.title: Conflict detected and merger guide generated
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Fixture branches with overlapping files trigger intersection detection and merger guide written to Obsidian.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Create fixture branches both touching server.js + src/runtime/contracts.ts. (2) Open two sessions, one per branch. (3) Wait for tick. (4) Merger guide present in Obsidian Polaris_Sessions/.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: No merger guide written; intersection not detected.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Merger guide in Polaris_Sessions/ with all template fields populated.

proofUnits.title: Merger guide written to correct Obsidian path
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Merger guide path uses the active project name read from CLAUDE.md, not a hardcoded value.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Run on Polaris: guide in Polaris_Sessions/. (2) Run on ScanMeNow: guide in scanmenow_Sessions/.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Guide always writes to a hardcoded path regardless of project.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Separate guide files in each project Sessions folder.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: Can test with Polaris only and verify path logic in skill file if second project unavailable.

proofUnits.title: Dependency-violation alert fires correctly
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Task moved to build-started with an unmerged blocking PR triggers an inline alert in the orchestrator session.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Set task A to build-started; task A has dependencies: [B]; task B has open unmerged PR. (2) Wait for BACKLOG:CHANGED tick. (3) Observe orchestrator session for alert.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Alert: Task A started before blocking task B (PR #N) is merged.

proofUnits.title: Pulsing glow visible on orchestrator card only
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Orchestrator session card has slowly pulsing amber-gold glow; all other session cards have no glow.
proofUnits.exactCommand: (1) Open Polaris with orchestrator + 2 build sessions. (2) DevTools: inspect .session-card[data-title="Project Orchestrator"]. (3) Confirm animation: orchestrator-pulse 2.5s ease-in-out infinite. (4) Inspect normal card: no animation.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: No animation on orchestrator card, or animation bleeds to other cards.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Orchestrator card pulses visibly; other cards static; animation confirmed in computed styles.
